question:
The coefficient matrix of the equations
$$2x+ky=7$$
$$x+2y=8$$
has determinant $3$.

(a) Determine the value of $k$.

(b) For this value of $k$, solve the equations using the inverse-matrix method.

(c) Verify the solution by matrix multiplication.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & k\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$|A|=4-k$$
Given that $|A|=3$,
$$4-k=3$$
Hence,
$$k=1$$

(b)
For $k=1$,
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
and
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus,
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}14-8\\-7+16\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}6\\9\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$x=2,\quad y=3$$

(c)
$$A\begin{bmatrix}2\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence, the solution is verified.
